Annotation.description: A declared fact about what a call reaches: `writes`, `emits`, and who said so.

kind.description: The declared edge kind, as the connector named it.

target.description: The other end: a declared node id, or a SCIP symbol string.

cached.description: True when this came from the cache rather than from a fresh run.

handle.description: The symbol this is the flow of, as a handle.

unknown.description: What the provider could not determine, and what cairn could not resolve.

FlowNode.description: One node of the answer: the provider's node, plus what cairn could resolve about it.

condition.description: The condition or the returned expression, as written. Display only.

declared.description:
What a connector declared about the call's target. A call into a generated
mutation reads `writes w17:entity/Order`, which is the sort of thing no call graph
can say.

handle.description: The handle of that symbol, so the next command can be run without a lookup.

name.description: What a call names, as written.

target.description:
The symbol a call resolved to. `null` for a call cairn could not resolve, which is
reported, and for every node that is not a call.

Stale.description: The staleness section of a JSON answer: `StaleFiles` plus the sentences text prints.

description:
One answer, as `--format json` prints it.

Borrowed from the envelope rather than owning a copy: this is built once, on the way
out, and an answer can carry a megabyte of body.

Generic in the payload for one reason: printing uses `serde_json::Value`, because the
envelope is built where the command is no longer known, while the published schema
has to name the command's own data type. One declaration, instantiated twice, so the
schema in `docs/json-schema/v1/` describes the object this actually prints.

body.description:
The text answer, exactly as text mode prints it above the envelope lines. The
three sections are fields here, so repeating them inside the body would be the
same claim twice and two places for it to drift.

command.description: The command that produced this, as it would be typed: `refs`, `for change`.

data.description: The answer as fields. `null` until the command has a data builder.

within.description: The declared container this answer was scoped to, or `null` for the whole index.
